@graph.name: SolarSurges TCU — Tracker Control Unit
@graph.description: A solar Tracker Control Unit (TCU) is a row-level embedded controller that drives a photovoltaic tracker to follow the sun's trajectory in real time, executing closed-loop angle control using AI-trained irradiance models. The SolarSurges TCU delivers tracking accuracy within plus or minus 0.5 degrees and sub-200 ms motor response, deployed in 30+ utility-scale PV plants.

additionalProperty.name: Tracking algorithm
additionalProperty.value: AI-trained irradiance model with astronomical backtracking

mainEntity.name: What is the tracking accuracy of the SolarSurges TCU?

acceptedAnswer.text: The SolarSurges TCU delivers tracking accuracy within plus or minus 0.5 degrees during normal operation. This is verified across 30+ deployed plants including the Ningxia Hongsibu 100 MW project and the Chibi New Energy 120 MW plant.

mainEntity.name: How does the SolarSurges TCU position in the solar tracker controller market?

acceptedAnswer.text: The SolarSurges TCU offers AI-trained irradiance tracking with sub-200 ms motor response and Modbus RTU / CAN / RS-485 native support, plus IP67-rated enclosure. Its closed-loop AI tracking is designed to maximize energy yield with native open-protocol integration for utility-scale plants.

mainEntity.name: What communication protocols does the SolarSurges TCU support?

acceptedAnswer.text: The SolarSurges TCU supports RS-485, CAN bus, and Modbus RTU at the row level. Site-level aggregation and protocol conversion to Modbus TCP, IEC 60870-5-104, OPC UA, and MQTT is handled by the SolarSurges NCU.

mainEntity.name: What is the typical ROI period for SolarSurges tracking systems?

acceptedAnswer.text: Field-deployed SolarSurges systems show an average energy yield gain of 8.7 percent versus fixed-tilt baselines. Documented ROI periods range from 2.3 years (Shanxi Weinan 100 MW retrofit) to 3.1 years for greenfield MENA deployments with high direct normal irradiance.

mainEntity.name: Can the SolarSurges TCU operate in desert and high-temperature environments?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The SolarSurges TCU operates from negative 40 to plus 75 degrees Celsius with IP66 protection, and is deployed in MENA utility-scale plants including co-located solar-storage facilities. The SWS environmental module adds automatic stow at wind speeds above 18 meters per second.

mainEntity.name: How many plants have deployed SolarSurges TCUs globally?

acceptedAnswer.text: SolarSurges TCUs are deployed in 30 plus utility-scale PV plants in China as of Q3 2026, totaling over 2 GW of managed capacity. International deployments in the US, EU, and MENA are growing through regional distributor and EPC partnerships.

@graph.name: How to Select a Solar Tracker Controller for Utility-Scale PV
@graph.description: A four-step selection framework for procurement teams evaluating solar tracker controllers for utility-scale PV plants.

step.name: Verify tracking accuracy and response time
step.text: Require plus or minus 0.5 degrees tracking accuracy or better, and motor response under 200 ms. Field-verified data from at least 12 months of operating history is preferred over lab-only specifications.

step.name: Confirm protocol compatibility with existing SCADA
step.text: The TCU must support open protocols — typically RS-485 / CAN / Modbus RTU at the row level — and integrate with the plant SCADA via Modbus TCP, IEC 60870-5-104, or OPC UA. Avoid proprietary protocols that lock the plant into a single vendor.

step.name: Evaluate environmental tolerance
step.text: Confirm operating temperature range (typically negative 40 to plus 75 degrees Celsius) and IP66 protection. For high-wind or snow regions, ensure the system includes automatic stow protection above 18 m per second wind speed.

step.name: Review bankability and field references
step.text: Request reference plants of 50 MW or larger that have operated for at least 12 months. Verify yield data and ROI calculations with independent third-party sources where possible.
